use: a quick money rule with a guess, from personal notes
request: My personal finance notes say this. Make a quick clip teaching the rule of 72 with one example and one for the viewer to try.

material.name: finance-notes.md
material.text:
Rule of 72: years to double = 72 / annual rate (%).
6% -> 12 years. 8% -> 9 years.
Only an estimate; works best for rates around 6-10%.

intent: Someone wants a quick mental trick for how long money takes to double.
goal: The viewer can use the rule of 72 on a new rate.
promise: A one-line trick for doubling time.
arc: The rule, a worked example, a guess with a pause, the answer.

events.text: Want to know how long money takes to double? Divide seventy-two by the yearly interest rate.
At six percent, seventy-two divided by six is twelve. Twelve years to double.
